newsitem.title: USA: Despite EVEREN cuts, Midwest muni firms see growth.
newsitem.headline: Despite EVEREN cuts, Midwest muni firms see growth.

text.p: Despite a sharp pullback from the municipal market last week by Chicago's EVEREN Securities Inc, executives at other Midwest muni firms said they do not expect to scale back their own operations.

Jonathan Savage, vice president and director of public finance at St. Louis-based AG Edwards & Sons Inc, said the firm is contemplating "careful growth" in California, as well as opening a new regional office.

The expansion, which echoed the cautious growth plans of several other Midwest muni firms, contrasts with EVEREN's announcement last week that it was slicing off its New York City and Boston municipal bond departments -- a move that will result in the loss of about 26 jobs.

EVEREN attributed the closings to a reconfiguring of its municipal operation to put it more in line with adverse market conditions. The closings followed the shuttering of other offices, as well as employee layoffs that have taken place over the last year.
Perrin Long, a securities industry analyst, said EVEREN's management may still be coping with the costs of last year's employee buyout of the firm from Kemper Corp.
"I think they are trying to get the thing more organized and structured," Long said.
But executives at other midwest-based firms said they do not expect to be consolidating operations and may entertain limited expansion.

Keith Kolb, a managing director of public finance at Robert W. Baird & Co. Inc., said the Milwaukee-based firm is in a "planned growth mode," which included opening a public finance office in Indianapolis in July. The firm already has public finance operations in Milwaukee and Chicago.
He added the firm is also exploring an expansion into another state, which he declined to name.

For Chicago's John Nuveen & Co Inc, the key to weathering current market doldrums has been to be "brain driven as opposed to brawn driven," said Clif Fenton, vice president and manager of the firm's investment banking division.
To that end, the firm had tried to come up with creative ways to structure or distribute deals, he said.

Fenton pointed to a recent $59 million Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs single-family mortage revenue bond issue the firm senior managed. That deal incorporated a collateralized mortgage obligation structure into a traditional muni housing deal, he explained.
He added the firm has added people in California and is contemplating some personnel additions in Chicago and New York in the institutional sales area.
Nelson D. Civello, director of the fixed-income group at Minneapolis-based Dain Bosworth Inc, said things are looking up in 1996 for the firm.
"We still think the markets are tepid to say the least," he said, adding however, that the firm's revenues are up and expenses are down from a year ago.
Just two years ago, Dain Bosworth acquired Chicago's Clayton Brown & Associates Inc, a move that resulted in layoffs and employee resignations as the two firms were melded together.
Civello said the firm was selectively adding staff, particularly salespeople.

AG Edwards's Savage said his firm continues to grow "because it is a brokerage firm with an investment banking division and not an investment banking firm with some brokers. Our mission is to deliver product."

Meanwhile, Friday's Chicago Tribune reported a rumor that Norwest Corp may be in the market to acquire Inter-Regional Financial Group Inc, the parent company of Dain Bosworth and Dallas-based Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc.
Spokespersons for Norwest and Inter-Regional Financial Group declined to comment Friday.
